messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The weather’s turned crisp — nice for a walk, but not much else happening on the streets. Heard the new bridge contract was approved last week; seems like everything’s moving forward as usual. Just don’t talk about it too long."
Sender 2: "The weather’s been strange lately—sun in the morning, rain by afternoon. Seemed like everyone was just… going about their days, same as always. Felt like the stillness was heavier than usual."
Sender 3: "Just got back from the market—everything’s busy, prices steady, even the usual crowd at the old noodle shop. Feels like normal, but the silence around certain topics is louder than ever. Be careful what you say, even to old friends."
Sender 4: "Just got back from the market — the bread’s still the same, but there’s a quiet kind of stillness in the air, like everyone’s holding their breath. Nothing’s changed on the surface, but I’ve started noticing how little people actually talk anymore."
Sender 5: "The air feels heavier than usual—everyone’s quiet, and it’s not just fear. The system’s working smoothly, too smoothly, like it’s been rehearsed. Best to keep things light, stay close, and watch how the quiet holds."
Sender 6: "The kids’ school’s back-to-school assembly went as usual today — no announcements, no tension, just the usual chatter. Feels like everyone’s settled into the rhythm, and honestly, it’s hard to imagine anything changing when even the smallest signs of unrest seem to vanish before they’re named."
Sender 7: "Just got back from the match—crowds were huge, everyone laughing, no tension at all. Feels like things are settling into a rhythm, quiet but stable. Nothing to worry about, really."
Sender 8: "The updates from the capital are quiet—no surprises, just the usual rhythm. Everything’s running on schedule, even the small things like the pension payments. Best to keep our plans simple and low-key for now."
Sender 9: "Just got word from someone in the finance district — they’re saying the system’s running smoother than it has in years, taxes collected on time, even the markets seem calm. Feels like everyone’s just waiting for something to happen, but nothing’s moving. Still, best to stay quiet for now."
Sender 10: "The streets are quiet, the markets are busy, and even the usual grumbling at work has gone flat — it’s like everyone’s stopped waiting for something to happen. Best to keep things simple, stay low, and trust the rhythm."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
